STEP 1 - Scene: This is a snack of whole raw almonds on a plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate is a square white one, roughly 22 cm across, about side-plate size. Its area is about 22 × 22 ≈ 480 cm² (square, so I used side × side rather than the circle formula).

STEP 3 - Items: Whole raw almonds, about 30 nuts.

STEP 4 - Area: The almonds cover about 12% of the plate, which is about 58 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is about 2 cm high, giving a gross volume of 58 × 2 ≈ 116 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: At a bulk density of about 0.6 (whole nuts with gaps between them), that gives about 70 g. A count check suggests less: roughly 30 almonds × 1.2 g each ≈ 36 g. The pile is mostly one layer with some stacking, so I'll settle on about 40 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds have about 580 kcal per 100 g, so 40 g × 5.8 ≈ 232 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 30 almonds weighing roughly 40 g and providing about 230 kcal is plausible for what is visible.
